introduction: A merge job rebases an agent's branch onto a target inside the workspace's repository and fast-forwards the target, running in the background and waiting its turn for the workspace. Batch rebase offers the same arithmetic synchronously over several branches at once.

glossary.batch rebase: A synchronous request that rebases each of several branches onto one target in turn, answering with a result per branch.
glossary.dead-lettered: A job that stopped making progress and was set aside, so that it can be requeued rather than retried for ever.
glossary.merge job: A queued job that rebases a source ref onto a target branch and fast-forwards the target to the result. It produces no merge commit.

requirements.title: What a merge job does
requirements.rationale: The job is the service's answer to merging agent branches by hand, so its semantics and its recorded outcome are what a person trusts instead of doing it themselves.

criteria.condition: a merge job runs and the rebase applies cleanly
criteria.action: rebase the source onto the target and fast-forward the target to the result
criteria.contract: the target branch afterwards holds the source's commits on top of the commits it had, with no merge commit; the job records the target's head before as base_sha and after as merged_sha

criteria.action: move a merge job through queued, running and then completed, failed, dead_letter or cancelled, recording its fields throughout
criteria.contract: the job carries id, workspace_slug, target_branch, source_ref, status, base_sha, merged_sha, conflict_files, error, retry_count, submitted_by, created_at and updated_at; base_sha and merged_sha are null until it completes and conflict_files is empty without a conflict

criteria.action: make a merge job wait its turn for the workspace's lock rather than refusing it for a busy workspace
criteria.contract: a job submitted while another operation holds the lock is still queued and runs once the lock frees; it is never answered 409 workspace_busy

criteria.condition: the rebase of the source onto the target conflicts
criteria.action: end the job as failed with the conflicting files recorded and leave the target branch where it was
criteria.contract: the job's status is failed, conflict_files names every conflicting path, and the target branch holds the head it had before the job ran

requirements.title: Submitting a merge job
requirements.rationale: The submit is where a duplicate or a non-existent branch has to be caught, because the job itself runs out of the caller's sight.

criteria.condition: a merge is submitted with a target branch and a source ref that both exist in a ready workspace
criteria.action: queue the job and answer with it
criteria.contract: HTTP 202 with the job at status queued, carrying its id, the target, the source and the submitting user

criteria.condition: a merge submit has a malformed body, a missing or invalid branch name, a workspace that is not ready, or a branch that does not exist
criteria.action: refuse the request and queue nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; the body is checked before the workspace, so a malformed branch name is 400 even for a workspace the caller cannot see

criteria.condition: a merge of the same source into the same target is already queued or running
criteria.action: refuse the request and queue nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type duplicate_merge; the existing job is unaffected and a merge of the same source into a different target is accepted

requirements.title: Following and undoing a job
requirements.rationale: A background job nobody can watch or stop is one an operator cannot recover from.

criteria.condition: a workspace's merge jobs are listed or one is read
criteria.action: return the jobs, at most 200, or the one named
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array, empty when there are none and never more than 200 entries, or with the single job; a job of another workspace and an unknown id are both HTTP 404

criteria.condition: a queued merge job is cancelled
criteria.action: cancel it so it never runs
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with status cancelled; the job does not run afterwards and the target branch is untouched

criteria.condition: a cancel names a job that is running, completed, failed, dead-lettered or already cancelled
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the job as it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 in the error envelope; the job's status is unchanged

criteria.condition: a dead-lettered merge job is requeued and no merge of the same source and target is queued or running
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the job at status queued; a job that is not dead-lettered, and one whose source and target are already queued or running, are both HTTP 409

requirements.title: Batch rebase
requirements.rationale: It answers while the caller waits, so its failure modes are the caller's problem rather than a job record's.

criteria.condition: a batch rebase is requested with a target ref and a list of branches
criteria.action: rebase each branch onto the target in turn while the request waits and answer with one result per branch
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a results array in the order the branches were given; each result is ok with the branch's new head, conflict with its conflicting files, or error

criteria.action: continue a batch rebase past a branch that conflicts or errors
criteria.contract: a batch where the second of three branches conflicts still reports results for all three, and the first and third are rebased

criteria.condition: a batch rebase has a malformed body, a missing target ref, an empty branch list, an invalid branch name, more than 20 branches, or a workspace that is not ready
criteria.action: refuse the whole request and rebase nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope, naming the offending branch by its index where there is one; the body is checked before the workspace; no branch is moved

criteria.condition: a batch rebase finds the workspace's lock held, or the rebase itself fails
criteria.action: refuse or fail the request without leaving a branch part way
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy for a held lock and HTTP 500 for a failed rebase; every branch is either at its new head or at the head it had before

requirements.title: Durability
requirements.rationale: A job lost to a restart is a merge an operator believes happened, which is worse than one that visibly failed.

criteria.condition: the component running a merge job restarts or is evicted
criteria.action: either complete the job or return it to the queue
criteria.contract: after the restart the job's status is one of queued, completed or failed, never running with nothing running it, and the job is never silently dropped

criteria.condition: a merge job makes no progress for 15 minutes
criteria.action: set it aside so it can be requeued rather than retried for ever
criteria.contract: the job's status becomes dead_letter and its retry count is recorded; a requeue then returns it to queued

criteria.action: leave the target branch either at the merged result or at the head it had before the job
criteria.contract: for a job interrupted at any point, the target branch holds one of those two heads and never an intermediate one

execution_paths.title: An agent's branch is merged into the target through the queue

steps.action: submits a merge of an agent's branch into the target branch
validates the body, confirms both branches exist and queues the job, answering 202
takes its turn for the workspace lock and starts the job
rebases the source onto the target and reports the result
polls the job to completed and reads the target's head before and after

execution_paths.title: A conflicting merge is recorded and the target left alone

steps.action: submits a merge of a branch that conflicts with the target
queues the job and starts it in its turn
reports the conflicting files and writes nothing
ends the job as failed with the conflicting files recorded
reads the job, sees the conflicting files, and finds the target branch at its previous head

execution_paths.title: Several branches are rebased in one request

steps.action: submits a batch rebase of three branches onto the target
takes the lock and rebases each branch in turn while the request waits
rebases two branches cleanly and reports a conflict on the third
receives three results in order: two new heads and one conflict with its files
